title: Hall's marriage theorem for bipartite matchings
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph whose vertex set admits a bipartition into parts $X$ and $Y$, so that every edge of $G$ joins a vertex of $X$ to a vertex of $Y$. For a set $S$ of vertices write $N(S) = \bigcup_{v \in S} N(v)$ for the union of the neighborhoods of the vertices in $S$. Then $G$ has a matching that saturates $X$ — a set of pairwise disjoint edges covering every vertex of $X$ — if and only if $\abs{S} \le \abs{N(S)}$ for every $S \subseteq X$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
G is bipartite with parts X and Y
quantified over all subsets S of X: |S| ≤ |N(S)| (Hall's condition)
conclusion: existence of a matching subgraph saturating X (X contained in its vertex set)
replaced:

Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with bipartition $(X, Y)$. Then $G$ contains a matching
that saturates every vertex in $X$ if and only if \[|N(S)| \geq |S| \quad \text{for all}
\quad S \subseteq X \qquad (5.2)\]
